summary.text: A chemical element is a kind of atom, defined by how many protons it has.
That proton count is the atomic number, and atoms of one element can still differ in their neutrons, which makes them isotopes.
The periodic table lists the elements by increasing atomic number, so each column shares recurring properties.

facts.label: Natural elements
facts.value: The first 94 occur naturally on Earth

facts.label: Oxygen
facts.value: Atomic number 8: eight protons in each atom

items.prompt: A lab adds two neutrons to an atom's nucleus and leaves its protons alone. What does the atom become?

options.label: An atom of the next element along
An atom of a synthetic element
Another isotope of the same element
A charged version of the same element

items.explain: The element is set by protons, so extra neutrons only make a different isotope of the same element.

items.prompt: Most elements never turn up as a pure nugget lying in the ground. In what form do nearly all naturally occurring ones exist?

options.label: Combined in compounds or mixtures
Locked inside single-element crystals
As free gases drifting in the soil
As separate protons in loose rock

items.explain: Fewer than twenty elements are sometimes found uncombined; nearly all others exist as compounds or mixtures.

items.prompt: A student says water must contain pockets of hydrogen gas and oxygen gas, since water is made of both elements. Is that right?

options.label: Yes, the gases sit as tiny bubbles inside it
Yes, but only once the water gets very hot
No, water has neither hydrogen nor oxygen
No, its molecules differ from those of the two gases

items.explain: Water consists of the elements hydrogen and oxygen, yet H₂O molecules are different from H₂ and O₂ molecules.

items.prompt: Inside a reactor, a nuclear reaction changes how many protons an atom has. What has happened to that atom?

options.label: It is the same element with a new weight
It has become an atom of a different element
It is the same element in a charged state
It has become an unstable copy of itself

items.explain: Nuclear reactions change an atom's atomic number, which turns it into an atom of a different element.

items.prompt: In the periodic table, elements are listed by increasing atomic number. What do the elements stacked in one column have in common?

options.label: The same number of neutrons
The same year of discovery
Recurring physical and chemical properties
The same natural abundance

items.explain: Columns, called groups, share recurring physical and chemical properties.

items.prompt: A newly named element has an atomic number of 110. Where did it come from?

options.label: Dug from rock as a native mineral
Left over from the Solar System's start
Formed by radioactive decay inside Earth
Made only artificially in nuclear reactions

items.explain: Elements beyond atomic number 94 have only been produced artificially by human-made nuclear reactions.
